About.title: About
About.summary:
I'm {name}, a frontend-focused fullstack developer based in South Jakarta with **{years}+ years** of professional experience. I'm currently the **sole frontend engineer across three AI products** — Knowledge Chat, Intelligent Document Processing and Credit Scoring — owning the UI architecture, the shared design system and the observability setup. Part-time, I build the frontend for **Medira**, an AI hiring platform. Before that I spent three years at **Infomedia Nusantara** (Telkom Indonesia group) building enterprise web apps.

My core is **React, Next.js and TypeScript**, and I work across the stack with **Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL and Docker** when a feature needs it. I also published an **IEEE paper** on CNN image classification, so I'm comfortable working alongside ML and data teams.

current.title: Frontend Developer
current.description:
Sole frontend engineer responsible for three AI products — Knowledge Chat, IDP (Intelligent Document Processing) and Credit Scoring — owning UI architecture end to end.
Built and maintained the shared design system and reusable UI component library (shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS) used across all three products.
Developed application UIs with React, Next.js (App Router), TypeScript and TanStack Query, coordinating closely with backend, product and QA to ship maintainable, well-tested features.
Set up application observability (OpenTelemetry SDK, OpenObserve, Pino structured logging) covering distributed tracing, RUM and custom product metrics; presented the findings to the wider engineering team.
Integrated the Qdrant vector database for a knowledge-base/RAG feature, including document ingestion, filtered search and cleanup workflows.

clovePaper.description: Detecting clove quality in Indonesia still relies on manual labor, so errors often occur when sorting cloves. The quality of cloves depends on good weather: unpredictable weather prolongs the drying process and leaves the cloves damaged and moldy. In this study, we use a CNN architecture with several combinations, namely the number of convolutions, the number of dense layers, and the size of the layers. The CNN architecture is trained using several variations of the color space and several variations of image segmentation to classify clove quality. This study used three color spaces (RGB, HSV, and YCbCr) and two segmentation methods (Otsu segmentation and HSV color segmentation). The best result is obtained using the HSV color space, the original dataset, and the E-5C-64LS-4D architecture, reaching 96% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-Score. To get a better model, we use the proper image segmentation method and compose a suitable color space to improve the CNN architecture's performance.
